img-2715-d77f6c8df1.title: Golden arches, translated
img-2715-d77f6c8df1.body: A very different take on the arches -- this sleek São Paulo Méqui looked nothing like home.

img-2723-ea912f258f.title: One horizon, endless city
img-2723-ea912f258f.body: Walking the skyline on foot, the concrete sea stretching in every direction -- Brazil starts loud.

img-2725-6305f2bb1d.title: The view from MASP
img-2725-6305f2bb1d.body: Looking out from MASP -- Sao Paulo's red museum on stilts -- toward a mural-wrapped building nearby, the city's street-art scene on full display.

img-2727-eb2812d5c2.title: Dinner, and a plan
img-2727-eb2812d5c2.body: A Brazilian steak dinner to remember at Figueira Rubaiyat -- picanha, ribeye, palm heart, and pitu shrimp piled high, the meal that set the tone for two weeks.

img-2735-e03fed57a0.title: The only way in
img-2735-e03fed57a0.body: Landed at Alta Floresta -- from here, the only way to Cristalino Lodge is by truck, then a transfer onto a boat for the final stretch up the river.

img-0949-9e499cb8db.title: Dwarfed by a tree
img-0949-9e499cb8db.body: Four of us barely wrap around the base of a centuries-old Brazil nut tree, one of the giants of the Cristalino.

dsc00036-81dc553603.title: Fifteen minutes in
dsc00036-81dc553603.body: A Harpy Eagle perched over the river -- one of the rarest raptors in the Amazon, spotted just fifteen minutes into our very first boat tour.

dsc00108-68fa341139.title: White against green
dsc00108-68fa341139.body: A snowy egret working the shallows along the Cristalino's clear water.

dsc00408-24fde0701c.title: Standing their ground
dsc00408-24fde0701c.body: A troop of spider monkeys shook branches and barked warnings, trying to scare us off their patch of canopy.

dsc00455-78e14aa97f.title: A wary eye
dsc00455-78e14aa97f.body: One of the spider monkey troop pausing mid-branch, keeping a wary eye on us below.

dsc00609-652830e408.title: Through the high canopy
dsc00609-652830e408.body: The spider monkey troop moved fast through the treetops -- our guide said some of the younger ones had never seen humans before and were more curious than afraid, pausing to watch us as we watched them.

dsc00870-9aac893b45.title: One more frame
dsc00870-9aac893b45.body: Out on the water at sunset, camera up, chasing the day's last good light.

img-2842-0201275b37.title: Into the canopy
img-2842-0201275b37.body: Our guide leading the way across the canopy walkway, high above the forest floor.

img-2900-878a1ef840.title: An unbroken sea of green
img-2900-878a1ef840.body: Sunrise from the Cristalino Lodge observation deck -- an unbroken carpet of rainforest stretching to the horizon.

dsc01309-84d5046951.title: The tree fills up
dsc01309-84d5046951.body: Neotropical cormorants and cattle egrets crowd a single tree at dusk, stacking up branch by branch.

img-2788-47b960163a.title: The sky catches fire
img-2788-47b960163a.body: The sky went orange right as the roost tree filled with birds -- one of the best sunsets of the trip.

img-2797-77884f33fb.title: Riding it in
img-2797-77884f33fb.body: Heading back to the lodge as the roost tree glowed behind us in the sunset.

dsc01370-c45906f0a8.title: Small things, big eyes
dsc01370-c45906f0a8.body: A tree frog found on low vegetation during a night walk, clinging to a leaf by its adhesive toe pads.

dsc01461-4fba8cad48.title: A stingless bee, a bromeliad in bloom
dsc01461-4fba8cad48.body: A stingless bee working a pink-coned aechmea in bloom -- one of a thousand tiny scenes at knee height in the Cristalino's understory.

dsc01907-9da0ea9960.title: The otter on the boulder
dsc01907-9da0ea9960.body: A neotropical otter hauled out on a midstream boulder, grabbing fish with its paws -- we watched it catch seven in a row, working the Cristalino's clearwater in low light.

dsc02014-38d46678fe.title: A turtle and its butterflies
dsc02014-38d46678fe.body: A yellow-spotted river turtle basking on a river rock, attended by butterflies and bees drinking its tears -- a hunt for minerals scarce in the Amazon.

dsc02088-d3bfbf1cf7.title: Boats at rest
dsc02088-d3bfbf1cf7.body: Lodge boats resting on the water as the forest went quiet for the night.

dsc02142-b9512dbadf.title: The mist lifts
dsc02142-b9512dbadf.body: Another look from the Cristalino Lodge observation deck, morning mist still clinging to the canopy.

img-2833-6183673d45.title: Right outside our door
img-2833-6183673d45.body: Returning from a hike, we found a capybara grazing a few feet from our room -- close enough to touch.

img-2858-f8c29392c9.title: Sand and clear water
img-2858-f8c29392c9.body: A quiet stretch of white-sand beach on the Cristalino -- shoes off, feet in the warm current.

dsc02187-8e320213a3.title: The elegant one
dsc02187-8e320213a3.body: A night encounter with an ocelot, the Pantanal's most elegant small cat -- chain-like rosettes smearing into long streaks.

dsc02271-9b4e43b866.title: Deer, with bird
dsc02271-9b4e43b866.body: A pampas deer doe crossing open grassland with a passenger -- a cattle tyrant riding her back for flushed insects.

dsc02339-7046609984.title: Tallest bird in the Americas
dsc02339-7046609984.body: A Jabiru stork -- the tallest flying bird in the Americas -- stalking wet grassland with its great upturned bill.

dsc02472-9377b7cd29.title: A cub in daylight
dsc02472-9377b7cd29.body: The headline of the trip: a six-month-old jaguar cub trailing close behind its mother, skittish of us in a way she wasn't.

dsc02518-ce2a3afa3c.title: Gardener of the forest
dsc02518-ce2a3afa3c.body: South America's largest land mammal -- known locally as the Brazilian tapir -- out and browsing in the open at midday. Notoriously shy and difficult to track, this was a rare, clear look at one.

dsc02568-35e7ef7c09.title: An eight-legged crossing
dsc02568-35e7ef7c09.body: A tarantula crossing the track during a safari drive through the Pantanal grounds.

dsc02602-a26a0ffd49.title: Silhouettes at sunset
dsc02602-a26a0ffd49.body: A flock of storks cut black against a burning orange Pantanal sunset.

dsc02811-bb805f4d09.title: The early bird gets the snake
dsc02811-bb805f4d09.body: Two southern crested caracaras in a tug-of-war over a snake -- technically part of the falcon family, but nothing like a typical falcon: bold, ground-striding opportunists that scavenge as much as they hunt.

dsc02834-20b5f5556f.title: Ancient and unbothered
dsc02834-20b5f5556f.body: A yacare caiman resting at the water's edge, close enough to count every scale.

dsc02889-eea7e2bdd2.title: Red, white and black
dsc02889-eea7e2bdd2.body: A yellow-billed cardinal atop a flowering shrub, crisp red, white and black -- despite the name, it's actually a tanager, not a true cardinal.

dsc02921-8268c02429.title: The largest kingfisher alive
dsc02921-8268c02429.body: A ringed kingfisher, the largest kingfisher in the Americas, framed through palm fronds above the water.

dsc03009-9bdef2895f.title: Jaws ajar
dsc03009-9bdef2895f.body: Another yacare caiman sunning in the wetland grass, jaws cracked open to cool down.

dsc03020-4a88f82645.title: Napping in the open
dsc03020-4a88f82645.body: A capybara stretched out and dozing in the grass, completely unfazed by our jeep.

dsc03028-ab3c086bd0.title: Waiting for a meal
dsc03028-ab3c086bd0.body: A trio of lesser yellow-headed vultures waiting on carrion, patient scavengers that quarter low over open country, sniffing out their next meal.

dsc03044-db26f9d1c4.title: The largest parrot alive
dsc03044-db26f9d1c4.body: A bonded pair of the world's largest flying parrot, cobalt from crown to tail, greeting each other at their nest box.

dsc03048-2c964dc19e.title: Two of a kind
dsc03048-2c964dc19e.body: A bonded pair of hyacinth macaws -- the world's largest flying parrot, cobalt from crown to tail -- perched together in a tree above the trail.

dsc03126-88b5051d8f.title: An armored shuffle
dsc03126-88b5051d8f.body: A six-banded armadillo shuffling through the evening grass, backlit by the low sun.

dsc03163-3cc1154027.title: Standing on a fence post
dsc03163-3cc1154027.body: A burrowing owl -- one that lives underground and hunts by day -- standing tall on a fence post in warm light.

dsc03373-b333a464af.title: The continent's largest deer
dsc03373-b333a464af.body: A marsh deer buck in full antler -- the continent's largest deer, and one of the Pantanal's Big Five alongside the jaguar, tapir and giant anteater.

dsc03598-34f873b708.title: Sneaking closer
dsc03598-34f873b708.body: A second jaguar sighting -- this time a pair. The female creeping quietly toward us through the grass, wary but drawing near, the much larger male trailing behind.

dsc03604-4beb5186b0.title: A few strides closer
dsc03604-4beb5186b0.body: The same jaguar, unbothered by the safari jeep, closing the distance step by step.

dsc03644-0c2df1f3b0.title: The big male, at rest
dsc03644-0c2df1f3b0.body: The large male settling into the grass -- a rare, close, calm portrait.

dsc03693-b9cefa2a24.title: Following her
dsc03693-b9cefa2a24.body: The male trailing after the female, intent on mating.

img-2943-a44dcc0191.title: Wetland gold
img-2943-a44dcc0191.body: The Pantanal's wetland lagoon glowing gold at sunset -- a quiet close to a wildlife-packed day.

img-2987-667ad4dec1.title: Copacabana, finally
img-2987-667ad4dec1.body: The mountains behind, the Atlantic in front -- our first view of Rio from the hotel balcony.

img-3012-f3f2f77e30.title: The city lit up gold
img-3012-f3f2f77e30.body: Rio's bay and skyline lit gold from the top of Sugarloaf Mountain at sunset.

img-3036-ff2e8b950a.title: At the feet of Christ the Redeemer
img-3036-ff2e8b950a.body: The whole family at the base of Christ the Redeemer, high above the city on Corcovado.

img-3045-pano-324cd55f7e.title: Rio, spread out below
img-3045-pano-324cd55f7e.body: A sweeping panorama from Corcovado -- beaches, bay, and mountains laid out in one frame.

img-3048-f69c034177.title: Together at the top
img-3048-f69c034177.body: The family at the summit platform, Christ the Redeemer towering just behind us.

img-3055-e7ec0d3edb.title: Almost straight up
img-3055-e7ec0d3edb.body: Standing right at the base of Christ the Redeemer atop Corcovado, looking straight up at its outstretched arms.

img-3099-588118d4f1.title: Copacabana at last light
img-3099-588118d4f1.body: Sunset over Copacabana Beach -- our first look at Rio, mountains behind, the Atlantic stretched out in front.
